legacy_root.answer: The 60% figure is TRACED to Kim et al. 2025 (arXiv:2506.07962) §3.2 / Figure 1(b) HELM: mean pairwise agreement WHEN BOTH MODELS ARE WRONG is 0.60, baseline 1/3 (uniform among 3 incorrect 4-choice options). HuggingFace analog is 0.423 vs chance 0.127. Same-company adds +0.022 on HELM (Table 1). The call sheet is a secondary source; 05-ECO is ABSENT on this Linux worktree. Treating 0.60 as Pearson rho of correctness is REFUTED (E3): the shared-draw map gives gamma=rho=0.40. Computed majority-error vs rho (n=9, p=0.7, beta-binomial): error 0.0988 at rho=0, 0.2642 at rho=0.40, 0.2870 at rho=0.60, 0.3000 at rho=1 (equals single-voter 0.3000). Among rules that use the ballots, majority degrades from the largest independent-voter gain down to the single voter; supermajority 2/3 is worse than a dictator on much of the interior; unanimity is worse until rho=1. Random dictator is FLAT (never used the other votes). When every participant is the SAME model at temperature 0, ALL anonymous rules collapse to one voter — majority-style is not defensible as social-choice diversity. It is only a noise average, and Apple 2026 plus Lefort 2024 show that even cross-family panels fail to beat the best individual once errors correlate.
legacy_root.canonical_mechanism: exchangeable beta-binomial Condorcet votes + shared-draw mixture for multiclass plurality; identical-ballot collapse at rho=1

legacy_root.evidence_tier_rule: E1 primary measurement or computation on this tree; E2 independent paper with effect AND baseline; E3 single secondary/call-sheet number; E4 inferred fetch. A headline number without its baseline is E3 and cannot promote a mechanism.

mechanisms.baseline_meaning: uniform draw among 3 incorrect options on 4-choice items (1/3)
mechanisms.claim: On HELM (71 models, 14,042 MMLU-style 4-choice items), mean pairwise agreement given both models are wrong is 0.60.
mechanisms.note: This is CONDITIONAL error-answer agreement, not Pearson rho of correctness indicators.

mechanisms.baseline_meaning: chance agreement among wrong options; mostly 10-choice items
mechanisms.claim: On HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard MMLU slice, mean agree-when-both-wrong is 0.423.

mechanisms.baseline_meaning: Helm regression intercept (mean pair, other covariates at reference)
mechanisms.claim: Same-developer pairs have higher HELM error-agreement than the intercept, coefficient +0.022.
mechanisms.section_or_figure: Table 1 Helm column, row Same Company

mechanisms.claim: The 05-ECO / call-sheet phrase '60%+ correlated errors' is a secondary paraphrase. Promoting 0.60 as pairwise correctness correlation rho is an overclaim.
mechanisms.note: Under the shared-draw mixture, P(same wrong|both wrong)=0.60 implies gamma=0.40, hence correctness-correlation rho=0.40, not 0.60. Headline number without that mapping is E3 and cannot promote a mechanism.

mechanisms.claim: For odd n and p>0.5 in the exchangeable beta-binomial model, majority error increases monotonically in rho and equals the single-voter error at rho=1.
mechanisms.effect_meaning: n=9 p=0.7: majority error 0.0988 at rho=0 vs 0.3000 at rho=1 (single-voter error 0.3000)

mechanisms.claim: When every participant emits the same ballot (same model, temperature 0, or gamma=1), every anonymous neutral voting rule — majority, plurality, Borda, IRV, Copeland — returns that ballot. No aggregator degrades less than another; they are identical to a single voter.
mechanisms.section_or_figure: limit rho=1 / identical profiles (computed check gamma=1 plurality error = 1-p)

mechanisms.claim: A 9-judge, 7-family LLM panel supplies about 2 effective independent votes; established aggregators close at most ~11% of the Condorcet gap; the best single judge matches or beats the panel.
mechanisms.effect_meaning: n_eff ≈ 2 vs nominal k=9; Condorcet gap 8-22pp

mechanisms.baseline: individual-model accuracy (paper: only marginal / no improvement)
mechanisms.claim: Lefort et al. 2024: majority vote over FinBERT, DistilRoBERTa, GPT-3.5, GPT-4 did not improve sentiment accuracy, consistent with failed independence.

Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) is majority over samples from one model. It can beat greedy decoding when residual sampling noise makes the mode more accurate than one draw. When the mode is a shared systematic error, majority amplifies it. That is not Condorcet independence.
mechanisms.note: Does not rescue same-model T=0 ensembles (gamma=1).
mechanisms.section_or_figure: method: sample-and-majority from a single LM

legacy_root.question: Social-choice theory assumes independent voters - when N participants share one model and therefore correlate their errors (the 05-ECO reject cites 60%+ correlated errors), which voting rule degrades least, and is any majority-style rule defensible at all?

reviewers.findings: 60% is TRACED to Kim et al. 2025 HELM agree-when-both-wrong with baseline 1/3. Call sheet is not the primary. 05-ECO absent here.

Did not re-judge the 60% primary. Independently: majority error rises in rho to the single-voter line; identical ballots collapse every anonymous rule; majority-style is not defensible as diversity when all participants are one model.

legacy_root.title: Determine which voting rules survive when every participant is the same model

voting_rule_verdict.least_degrading_including_dictator: random dictator (flat, no gain to lose)
voting_rule_verdict.reason: Same-model temperature-0 copies produce identical ballots. Anonymous aggregators cannot outperform the single model. At the TRACED Kim statistic (gamma=0.40, not rho=0.60) a 9-voter majority still has only 3.58pp lift over one voter under the beta-binomial, and Apple 2026 finds even a 9-family-diverse panel fails to beat the best individual. Majority is defensible only as self-consistency against residual sampling noise, and that fails when the mode is a shared error.
